newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Cosatu postpones May 12 strike.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Cosatu postpones May 12 strike.

text.p: The Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) has postponed its planned nationwide strike, planned for May 12, until June 2, following an earlier court ruling against the action, state radio reported on Friday.
South Africa's Labour Appeal Court ruled against the May 12 strike because labour had failed to give sufficient notice under the terms of the Labour Relations Act.
The radio quoted a regional Cosatu offical as saying that the only way business could stop the planned action next month would be to grant workers their demands.
Cosatu called the protest action over the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill which has threatened to become a flashpoint between trade unions and business.
The bill was approved by cabinet in April and is now before the tri-partite National Economic Development and Labour Council (Nedlac) for discussion.
Cosatu wants to ensure its demands relating specifically to a 40-hour working week and six months paid maternity leave are not watered down when the bill is eventually tabled in parliament.
